classification.difficultyReason: Track composition through two replacements, recognising that the second removal contains both juices in the current mixture proportions, then reconstruct and simplify the final ratio.

content.prompt: A container is filled with 64 L of orange juice, then 12 L of juice are removed and the container is topped up with lemon juice. The juice is thoroughly mixed before 12 L of the mixture is removed and the container is again topped up with lemon juice. What is the ratio of orange juice to lemon juice in the final mixture?

answer.short:
$169:87$ (orange juice to lemon juice).

The second removal takes away the same fraction of each juice as its fraction of the thoroughly mixed contents.
answer.worked:
After the first removal and refill, there are $64-12=52$ L of orange juice and $12$ L of lemon juice. Thorough mixing means that $\frac{52}{64}=\frac{13}{16}$ of the next amount removed is orange juice.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Orange juice removed next}&=12\times\frac{13}{16}\text{ L}\\\text{Orange juice removed next}&=\frac{39}{4}\text{ L}\\\text{Final orange juice}&=52-\frac{39}{4}\text{ L}\\\text{Final orange juice}&=\frac{169}{4}\text{ L}\\\text{Final lemon juice}&=64-\frac{169}{4}\text{ L}\\\text{Final lemon juice}&=\frac{87}{4}\text{ L}\\\text{Orange juice : lemon juice}&=\frac{169}{4}:\frac{87}{4}\\\text{Orange juice : lemon juice}&=169:87\end{align*}$$
